title: vpc: provision private control-plane networking (subnets, endpoints, SGs, peering, DNS)
author: Priya Nair
description:
Motivation: enable automated provisioning of the Private Control Plane networking surface for VPC-based private deployments. This PR adds Terraform modules and installer hooks to create isolated control-plane subnets, interface endpoints for required AWS services, security groups with least-privilege rules, VPC peering route automation for customer VPCs, and DNS setup (Route53 private hosted zones + conditional forwarding). It also wires up the installer and helm chart to use the provisioned endpoints and provides upgrade/rollback plans for existing customers.

Summary of changes: adds a new terraform/modules/control-plane module (subnets, route tables, endpoints, SGs, route53), expands terraform/modules/network to support peering connections and peering route automation, updates helm chart values schema for private-endpoint discovery, adds installer preflight and migrate scripts to detect existing control plane networking and perform in-place migration or safe rollback, and extensive docs and examples (example/terraform/private-control-plane). Includes acceptance tests (terraform plan & apply in isolated account simulation) and updates to the private-installer README.

Checklist:
- [x] Terraform module for control-plane networking (subnets, route tables, endpoints)
- [x] Security group templates and lint rules
- [x] VPC peering automation with route propagation and tag-based discovery
- [x] Route53 private hosted zone + conditional forwarding option
- [x] Helm chart changes to consume endpoint hostnames/IPs and CSP-aware defaults
- [x] Installer preflight + migrate/rollback scripts
- [x] Integration tests and CI pipeline steps
- [x] Docs and upgrade notes

Notes: the implementation favors conservative defaults (private subnets across 2 AZs, endpoints for s3, sts, ecr, kms, ssm, ec2, iam where relevant), and exposes configuration knobs for customers who need different coverage. The migration path will not delete resources unless `--force` is supplied; rollback is implemented by saving a snapshot of created resources and re-applying previous Terraform state where possible. For on-prem air-gapped installs, the installer will still create local DNS forwarding entries but will skip cloud endpoints.

References: Linear ENG-9812 (private control plane provisioning), ENG-10005 (installer upgrade path).

ci_log_summary: Initial CI run: terraform plan failed due to missing CI plan-role; post-fix rerun passed all checks. Integration tests use a mocked AWS account sandbox and validate endpoint provisioning and route propagation logic.
merge_outcome: Squash and merge by Maya Chen — merged commit message consolidated module notes, migration instructions, and upgrade checklist.
upgrade_notes: When enabling control-plane provisioning for an existing private deployment: 1) run installer preflight (checks for overlapping CIDRs and existing endpoints), 2) run terraform apply in dry-run mode and review proposed peering routes, 3) apply during maintenance window to allow DNS TTL propagation (recommended 5–10 minutes), 4) if rollback is required, run installer rollback which will restore previous terraform state snapshots. See docs/private-deploy/control-plane.md for full playbook.
release_notes: Added automated private control-plane provisioning: Terraform module for control-plane networking, VPC peering automation, Route53 private zone support, installer migration/rollback tools, and helm chart updates for private endpoint consumption.
migration_plan: 1) run preflight_check.sh to detect conflicts; 2) terraform plan with the new modules in a staging account; 3) run migrate_control_plane.sh --apply to perform staged provisioning; 4) run helm upgrade pointing to the new endpoints; 5) validate connectivity and service health; 6) if issues, run rollback_control_plane.sh to revert to previous state.
notes_for_ops: This module creates interface endpoints for SSM/ECR/S3/KMS/STS and will create route entries for peered VPCs. Ensure the account has quotas for endpoints and peering connections. The default SGs are least-privileged; audit them against your org requirements. For cross-account peering, ensure accept permissions are configured or use the provided accept-peering helper.
risk_and_mitigation: Risk: accidental overlapping CIDRs or creating peering routes that conflict with customer route tables. Mitigation: preflight CIDR checks, opt-in peering creation, explicit depend_on in Terraform to avoid partial apply, and non-destructive defaults with explicit --force for destructive operations.
follow_up: Follow-up tasks tracked in Linear ENG-10112: add Azure/GCP provider parity for control-plane endpoints and ENG-10113: automated tests in a multi-account integration harness.
